hypotheses.claim: Removing hyphen from ordinary identifier lexing is sufficient to eliminate the observed tight-vs-spaced subtraction/arrow ambiguity in the current D candidate without changing G9 semantic concepts.
hypotheses.evidence: 20,000 matched spacing cases: current D 2,480 differences, repaired candidate 0; repaired G9/Dialect proxy parses.
hypotheses.falsifier: A larger normative corpus reveals required hyphenated identifiers that cannot be migrated reversibly or a new lexical ambiguity remains.

hypotheses.claim: Operator alternative aliases are a lower-risk way to preserve operator identity in canonicalizer input than a single high-priority OPERATOR terminal.
hypotheses.evidence: 16/16 symbolic operators distinct after aliasing; single high-priority OPERATOR negative control steals declaration '=' and rejects import syntax.
hypotheses.falsifier: Normative parser/AST construction retains exact operator identity with a simpler representation and no declaration-token collision.

hypotheses.claim: A contextual typed expression-bodied fn_decl can expose prior definition-to-call semantics without perturbing the admitted repaired G9/Dialect corpus.
hypotheses.evidence: Legacy repaired tree hashes unchanged by fn extension; 5,000 formatting variants stable; 5,000 valid composed bindings resolved and 3,000 invalid cases rejected.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production parser/type-effect/compiler or Qwen-reader benchmark finds ambiguity, semantic drift, unacceptable repair burden, or existing constructs provide equivalent closure.

hypotheses.claim: CC-WP-02 should require whitespace-robust lexical equivalence and explicit operator identity before ProgramSemanticId is minted.
hypotheses.evidence: Default parse-tree hashing can collapse distinct operators and lexical spacing can change current D tree meaning.
hypotheses.falsifier: A normative canonicalizer proves those source distinctions are recovered deterministically from a lower layer before semantic identity without parser changes.

counterhypotheses.claim: Hyphenated ordinary identifiers are valuable enough that lexer restriction is worse than requiring separator rules or escaping.
counterhypotheses.test: Run full corpus/archives and target-reader migration benchmark over strict identifiers versus an explicit escape/raw-identifier design.

counterhypotheses.claim: No source-level fn declaration is needed because existing rule/cycle/Needle constructs already lower to reusable typed calls without escape hatches.
counterhypotheses.test: Compile reusable functions through the normative production pipeline before adopting fn_decl.
